obtained.how: not obtained. Read instead, as an intermediary only: Erkkilä et al. 2018, Biogeosciences 15: 429–445 (open access), which restates the Tedford et al. 2014 dissipation and gas-transfer model

bibliography.note: Crossref: Tedford, MacIntyre, Miller, Czikowsky (2014), J. Geophys. Res. Oceans 119(8): 4689–4713 — matches the citation

claims.claim: night convection alone sustains about 0.55–0.93 m d⁻¹ (k600) for heat losses of 25–200 W m⁻² (project computation after Tedford et al. 2014)
claims.note: Tedford's own text not read. Through the intermediary (Erkkilä et al. 2018, Eq. 5 and 8: ε = c1·u*w³/(κz) + c2·|β| when cooling, c2 = 0.77; k = c4·(εν)^¼·Sc^−½, c4 = 0.5; β = g·αt·Heff/(ρw·Cp)), the project's arithmetic reproduces 0.55, 0.65, 0.78 and 0.93 m d⁻¹ at 25, 50, 100 and 200 W m⁻² for calm water with αt = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ and ν = 0.955 × 10⁻⁶ m² s⁻¹ (22 °C), ρw = 998, Cp = 4186 — so the formulation as Erkkilä states it gives the paper's numbers. Whether Tedford's paper prints these constants in this form is unchecked.

claims.claim: a convective floor of 0.34–0.93 m/day at 25–200 W/m² of heat loss (Read et al. 2012, Tedford et al. 2014)
claims.note: The range spans two formulations (oxygen_metabolism.md §1): Read et al. 2012's constants give 0.34–0.57 m/d and Tedford's (via Erkkilä) 0.55–0.93 m/d over the same heat losses; the comment merges the low end of one with the high end of the other. The paper's §3.1.6 gives only the Tedford range.

notes: Recommend the paper cite the formulation as 'Tedford et al. 2014, as applied by Erkkilä et al. 2018' unless the human fetches Tedford and confirms c2 = 0.77, c4 = 0.5 and z = 0.15 m there. Erkkilä et al. applied the model on humic Lake Kuivajärvi, Finland, in September 2014; they credit z = 0.15 m to Tedford et al. 2014 and Mammarella et al. 2015. The 22 °C water properties make the computation a summer-night value: in 10 °C autumn water (αt ≈ 0.9 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹, ν ≈ 1.31 × 10⁻⁶ m² s⁻¹; standard values, project arithmetic) the same heat loss gives ~14 % less.
